key_insight: The paper shows that quantum machine learning can be made both computationally efficient and privacy-preserving by transpiling general quantum circuits into blind brickwork graphs with provable depth and width bounds.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical route to estimate and minimize the qubit, depth, and compilation overhead needed for near-term blind quantum computing implementations of QML workloads.
method: Built MasonQ, a universal transpiler that converts arbitrary quantum circuits into computational brickwork graph states.
Derived asymptotic upper bounds for UBQC brickwork depth, showing scaling as O(ωn) with circuit width ω and gate complexity n.
Applied the transpiler to representative B-QML circuits including QFT, HHL, recommendation systems, and quantum transformers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and resource estimates, including an optimality result up to logarithmic corrections and a proposed 12-qubit minimal blind B-QML implementation.
watch_item: The results are largely asymptotic and resource-estimate based, so real hardware noise, compilation constants, and measurement overhead may affect practical performance.
paper_title: On the Computational Complexity of Blind Quantum Machine Learning
